one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-03 to 2026-11-01. AAOI's own Q3 report is not expected inside the window: it has reported Q3 on the first Thursday-ish of November (Nov 6 in 2025), so likely ~Nov 5, 2026. The 1.6T ramp and Q3 revenue ($255-290M guide) are therefore unresolved in-window. In-window industry events: Chinese module makers' Q3 reports (Innolight/Eoptolink, by Oct 31) and hyperscaler Q3 prints with capex guides (late October) - both read-through events that move optical names as a group, direction unknown but capex has kept being raised (Amazon guide raised to $220B). Overhang: the $600M ATM filed Aug 21 is still being sold into the market, a mild negative drift. No reliable post-earnings drift signal (Q2 was a mixed print and the stock is ~50% off its high). I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on $115.59 with a 1% negative tilt for ATM supply and a monthly sigma of 0.37 (139% annual / ~3.5, slightly trimmed), giving P(>=115.59)=0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% P/E (FY2028E EPS $5.50 x 20x = $110) and 40% EV/EBITDA (FY2028E EBITDA $850M x 15x + ~$0.3B net cash over ~97M diluted shares = $135); multiples sit at the low end of a 10-name optical/AI-connectivity peer set next to the pure transceiver makers (Innolight ~18x, Eoptolink ~20x, Fabrinet 25x).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028E EPS $5.50 x 20x (valuation at Oct-2027 looks one year forward)

inputs_detail.derivation: $4.60 x ~1.20: unit capacity grows from ~650k/month (end-2026) to ~930k/month (end-2027) per management (+43%), haircut for annual ASP declines on 800G/1.6T that Innolight itself concedes (rational price cuts), and ~6% ATM dilution

Peer median fwd P/E ~36.7x (range 18-62x). AAOI placed beside the direct transceiver makers (Innolight ~18x, Eoptolink ~20x) and below Fabrinet (25.5x) because its non-GAAP GM is ~30% vs Innolight 46%/Coherent ~40%/Lumentum 50%, FCF is deeply negative (H1 op cash flow -$74M, capex $335M), and one customer (Digicomm, CATV) is 43% of H1 revenue
84.9M outstanding Aug 20 + ~5.6M from $600M ATM at ~$108 + convert/RSU dilution; Q3 guide already uses 92.8M

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY2028E EBITDA $850M x 15x = $12.75B EV + ~$0.3B net cash = $13.05B / 97M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Revenue consistent with $4.60 EPS at ~30-32% GM and ~$250M opex; vs FY2026 ~$1.1B target, 1.6T ramp ($200M+ orders, >$70M Q4) and CATV >$325M/yr
FY2027E EBIT ~$560M + D&A ~$120M = ~$680M (26% margin), grown ~25% with capacity to 930k units/month
Bottom of peer fwd EV/EBITDA range (15-96x, median ~42x), level with Innolight (~15x) and below Fabrinet (22.5x) for the margin/FCF/concentration reasons above
June-30 cash $508.8M less debt $186.4M = $322M; +$600M ATM roughly offset by H2-2026 capex/working-capital burn

bear.story: 1.6T qualification/yield slips or a hyperscaler cuts orders; DSP/TIA shortages cap shipments while Chinese makers (cheaper, 46% GM) take share and price 800G down; GM stays <30%, more ATM dilution; 2027 EPS ~$2-2.5 at ~22x. AI capex digestion in 2027 would compound it.

base.story: Ramp roughly as guided: FY2026 ~$1.1B, FY2027 ~$2.5B, EPS ~$4.5; market values on FY2028 EPS ~$5.5 at ~20-22x in line with transceiver peers; CATV steady at ~$325M+ through Dell'Oro's 2027 cable outside-plant peak.

bull.story: Shortage persists into 2027 (LightCounting: could extend if GPU output beats), AAOI's US-made capacity (930k/month, >50% Texas) and in-house lasers win share with hyperscalers seeking non-China supply; GM moves to mid-30s and FY2028 EPS reaches ~$8-9 at ~25x, revisiting the $234 high.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 18x (Innolight) to 62x (Astera Labs); fwd EV/EBITDA ~15x to ~96x. US peer fwd EV/EBITDA figures are approximations: trailing EV/EBITDA scaled by trailing/forward revenue (constant-margin assumption); Chinese peers' figures are judgment from consensus net income and market cap.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 20x fwd P/E and 15x fwd EV/EBITDA: inside the range, at the low end, beside the two pure-play transceiver makers and below the median by ~45%. On the street's FY2027 EPS of $4.60, today's $115.59 is ~25x, i.e. already in the lower half of the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount to the median, not a premium, and expected to persist through the horizon: (1) structurally lower gross margin (~30% non-GAAP vs 37-75% for peers, 46% at Innolight on the same product); (2) negative FCF and repeated ATM raises (three in 2026, ~$1.7B) that keep diluting; (3) concentration (Digicomm 43% of H1 revenue, 67% of receivables; a single hyperscaler >10%); (4) assembly-heavy model closer to Fabrinet than to component/semis peers. The higher-margin semis (MRVL, CRDO, ALAB, MTSI) are included for end-market exposure but are an upper bound, not a target.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$62 the market would be valuing AAOI at ~13x FY2027 consensus EPS or pricing 2027 earnings near $2.5, which would most likely mean the 1.6T ramp failed qualification/yields, a hyperscaler pulled orders, or 800G pricing collapsed - a fundamental break, not ordinary 139%-vol noise (a ~1-sigma monthly move from here only reaches ~$80).

key_uncertainties: Whether AAOI keeps hyperscaler share against Innolight/Eoptolink as shortages ease (LightCounting expected easing by end-2026) and pricing normalises
Gross-margin trajectory: ~30% today vs 40-50% at peers; scale benefits vs ASP declines
Further dilution from ATM programs and capex-heavy expansion
DSP/TIA supply (management's named bottleneck) capping 2027 shipments
AI capex durability into 2027-28 and CPO adoption reducing pluggable content
CATV revenue cliff after the 2027 cable outside-plant peak and Digicomm concentration
reasoning: Industry evidence is uniformly strong on demand: LightCounting has Ethernet transceivers +65% in 2026 with demand ~30% above supply (InP EML limited); Coherent datacom +59% y/y, Lumentum +109% y/y with 50% GM; Innolight H1 revenue +182% and orders extending into 2027; hyperscaler capex still being raised. So AAOI's stated constraint (capacity, DSP/TIA) is credible, and its US/Taiwan capacity is a share opportunity. But the chain also says pricing will fall 'at a rational rate', Innolight earns 46% GM on the same product vs AAOI's 30%, and Innolight itself de-rated ~40% from June despite record earnings, i.e. the market is already discounting cycle/CPO risk across the group. AAOI adds negative FCF, three ATMs in 2026 and heavy customer concentration. Valuing FY2028E EPS $5.50 at 20x and EBITDA at 15x (bottom of a 10-peer set, next to Innolight/Eoptolink) gives ~$120, essentially today's price; consensus FY2027 EPS $4.60 puts the stock at ~25x. Scenarios: bear $55 (30%), base $122 (45%), bull $225 (25%), each a lognormal with 28-40% dispersion; the mixture has median ~$118 and mean ~$130, and its 12-month spread (~±70% interquartile in log terms) is narrower than the 139% realized vol implies, because realized vol was inflated by the 2026 parabolic move and I expect earnings delivery to anchor it somewhat - still far wider than the ±25-35% large-cap base rate. Research was limited to ~20 queries; Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits), so peer multiples come from stockanalysis.com pages and the US-peer forward EV/EBITDA and Chinese-peer multiples are approximations.
